{{Short description|Feature of certain mathematical spaces}}
In [[mathematics]], the notion of being '''compactly embedded''' expresses the idea that one set or space is "well contained" inside another. There are versions of this concept appropriate to general [[topology]] and [[functional analysis]]. The notation for "<math>X</math> is compactly embedded in <math>Y</math>" is <math>X \subset\subset Y</math>, or <math>X \Subset Y</math>.

When used in functional analysis, compact embedding is usually about [[Banach spaces]] of functions.

Several of the [[Sobolev inequality|Sobolev embedding theorems]] are compact embedding theorems.

When an embedding is not compact, it may possess a related, but weaker, property of [[Cocompact embedding|cocompactness]].

==Definition==

=== Topological spaces ===
Let <math>X</math> be a [[topological space]], and let <math>V</math> and <math>W</math> be [[subset]]s of <math>X</math>. We say that <math>V</math> is '''compactly embedded''' in <math>W</math> if
* <math>V \subseteq \operatorname{Cl}(V) \subseteq \operatorname{Int}(W)</math>, where <math>\operatorname{Cl}(V)</math> denotes the [[Closure (topology)|closure]] of <math>V</math>, and <math>\operatorname{Int}(W)</math> denotes the [[Interior (topology)|interior]] of <math>W</math>; and
* <math>\operatorname{Cl}(V)</math> is [[Compact space|compact]].
For [[Hausdorff spaces]], this is equivalent to there existing some compact set <math>K</math> such that <math>V \subseteq K \subseteq \operatorname{Int}(W)</math>.

=== Normed spaces ===
Let <math>X</math> and <math>Y</math> be two [[normed vector space]]s with norms <math>\| \cdot \|_X</math> and <math>\| \cdot \|_Y</math> respectively, and suppose that <math>X \subseteq Y</math>. We say that <math>X</math> is '''compactly embedded''' in <math>Y</math>, if
* <math>X</math> is [[continuously embedded]] in <math>Y</math>; i.e., there is a constant <math>C</math> such that <math>\|x\|_Y \le C \|x\|_X</math> for all <math>x</math> in <math>X</math>; and
* The embedding of <math>X</math> into <math>Y</math> is a [[compact operator]]: any [[bounded set]] in <math>X</math> is [[totally bounded]] in <math>Y</math>, i.e. every [[sequence]] in such a bounded set has a [[subsequence]] that is [[Cauchy sequence|Cauchy]] in the norm <math>\| \cdot \|_Y</math>.

=== Banach spaces ===
If <math>Y</math> is a [[Banach space]], an equivalent definition is that the embedding operator (the identity) <math>i \colon X \to Y</math> is a [[compact operator]].
